title: Psalm 129: Plowed Over, but Not Overcome
summary: Israel is called to declare that it has been attacked over and over since its youth, its back plowed like a field, yet its enemies have never prevailed, because the righteous LORD cut the cords of the wicked. The psalm then prays that those who hate Zion will wither like grass on a rooftop, useless for any harvest, with no one passing by to bless them.

from.text: Psalm 120 opens the Songs of Ascents, a collection of fifteen short psalms (120 to 134) that each carry the heading

line: Israel says it has been attacked since its youth, its back plowed like a field, yet its enemies never prevailed, because the LORD cut the cords of the wicked.
guide: Many people carry long scars from years of mistreatment. The psalm does not call the wounds small, but it says the cords were cut. Look back and name where God brought an end to something that might have destroyed you.

care.text: Verses 5 to 8 pray that those who hate Zion come to nothing. This is a mild example of the cursing psalms. It asks that their hatred fail, not that blood be shed. The book page's part on the cursing psalms sets out how Christians read such prayers. No reading of it makes it right to harm anyone, and it names no people of today.

stanzas.title: The plowed back and the cut cords
May Zion's haters wither like rooftop grass

verses.t: A song of ascents. Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth— let Israel now declare—
many a time they have persecuted me from my youth, but they have not prevailed against me.
The plowmen plowed over my back; they made their furrows long.
The LORD is righteous; He has cut me from the cords of the wicked.
May all who hate Zion be turned back in shame.
May they be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it can grow,
unable to fill the hands of the reaper, or the arms of the binder of sheaves.
May none who pass by say to them, “The blessing of the LORD be on you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”
